title: Systems that prompt your AI — DB-driven loops with skills and cron
summary: Riffs on Boris Cherny's advice to build loops that prompt Claude instead of prompting it yourself: connect the AI to a database with work and issues tables, use cron jobs to detect pending changes, and run skills for scoping, implementing, testing and repeating until the human goal is met. Counterpoint: for go-to-market work the human is still the bottleneck and must stay in the loop.
takeaways: Queue work in DB tables and let scheduled skills pick it up.
Chain scope, implement, test skills until a goal check passes.
Creative/GTM tasks still need a human checkpoint.

title: StopSlop — a Claude skill file that strips AI writing tells
summary: StopSlop is a GitHub skill file that bans filler phrases, throat-clearing openers, emphasis crutches and adverbs so Claude's copy stops sounding like Claude. The creator finds it removes most tells but notes the deeper problem: AI prose lacks a position, so the last 20% still needs a human voice.
takeaways: Drop a banned-patterns skill into your writing workflow.
Deleting tells doesn't add opinion; take a stance yourself.
Use AI for the first 80%, edit the last 20% by hand.

title: Claude Code Meta ads pipeline — Arcads API, Ads MCP and an Airtable swipe file
summary: Setup for having Claude Code generate and launch static Meta ads: clone the creator's GitHub repo in Claude Desktop's code tab, give it an Arcads.ai API key, add the Facebook/Meta Ads MCP as a custom connector, hand it an Airtable database of 2,000 example ads, have it ask 20 questions about your offer, pick 50 concepts, and upload creatives by cloning settings from an existing ad ID. Claims $30k revenue at 10-50 cents per image.
takeaways: Give the agent a database of proven ads as reference, not just a brief.
Make it ask ~20 questions about your offer before generating.
Clone an existing ad's settings by ID so uploads don't break targeting.

title: Vibe-coded landing page toolkit — seven tools for real design taste
summary: Toolkit for better AI-built landing pages: 21st.dev components, getdesign.md to borrow famous design systems, WebGPU for heavy web animation, impeccable.style design prompts, a repo for recreating any landing page, awesome-design to break down brand design blocks, and a repo that 'gives Claude taste'. Last two repos are unnamed.
takeaways: Feed the agent a real design system file instead of 'make it pretty'.
Pull prebuilt components from 21st.dev to raise baseline quality.
impeccable.style prompts give AI UIs stronger design judgment.

title: Mixed-reality infinite canvas — directing Claude Code agents from Quest 3
summary: Early demo of an XR infinite canvas on Meta Quest 3 synced with a desktop canvas: drop reference images into a sphere, put your hand in it and speak a request (e.g. components visualizing multi-agent progress), make a fist to send it to Claude Code agents under custom orchestration, and watch results build up in place.
takeaways: Spatial containers are a neat metaphor for scoping agent context.
Gesture-to-send keeps hands-free XR workflows fluid.
Next frontier: point at objects and describe changes in place.

title: Claude Code simple mode — ablating system prompts makes the model smarter
summary: Boris Cherny at YC Startup School: Claude Code accepts --system-prompt for a custom system prompt, and an undocumented simple mode (env var CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1) deletes all system and tool prompts. Anthropic uses it as an ablation and finds the model is slightly more intelligent without them, though product prompts still help it behave as users expect.
takeaways: Ablate your own agent prompts to see which instructions actually help.
Over-instruction can cap model capability; keep prompts minimal.
Try simple mode for raw-capability tasks where product guardrails aren't needed.

title: Hugging Bay — torrent index for open LLM weights
summary: Hugging Bay is a Pirate Bay-style site for downloading open model weights via BitTorrent, pairing with torrent CLIs to pull large models without hammering a single host.
takeaways: Torrents spread bandwidth for multi-hundred-GB weight downloads.
Verify checksums against the official release.

title: Attention-directing web design — spacing, contrast and pacing as persuasion
summary: Caption-only essay: premium websites control attention through spacing, contrast, motion and pacing, deciding what you notice, where you pause and when you click, which makes the brand feel more valuable and trustworthy. Mood reference; the video has no instructional audio.
takeaways: Design is about what to reveal, remove and when.
Whitespace builds focus; transitions build momentum.

title: Nine UI design languages — feeding style guides to Manus
summary: Sponsored Manus post listing design languages used to vibe-code sites: skeuomorphism, neumorphism, glassmorphism, claymorphism, minimalism, maximalism, brutalism, liquid glass and spatial UI, fed as a design guide plus prompts to the Manus agent.
takeaways: Naming a specific design language gives AI builders a clear target.
Paid Manus partnership (#ad).

title: Kimi K3 — hyped open-weight 2.8T model claims to beat Fable 5 cheaply
summary: Hype clip claiming Moonshot's Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters, open source) beat Claude Fable 5 on coding and design at ~5x lower cost, rattled the Nasdaq, and built a CS:GO portal clone for ~$3 in tokens. No benchmarks shown; link gated behind a comment.
takeaways: Price-performance pressure from open-weight models is real; verify claims.
Market-moving claims here are unsourced.

title: Claude Code website remix — clone and combine sites from URLs
summary: Paste URLs of sites you like into Claude Code and ask it to clone and merge elements (Apple's animation, Stripe's pricing, Airbnb's design), then improve copy and add sections. Thin pitch; tutorial gated behind a comment.
takeaways: Reference URLs give the agent concrete design targets.
Respect copyright when cloning others' sites.

title: Prime Agent — self-rewriting harness lifts Opus 5 to 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3
summary: Prime Intellect released Prime Agent, an open-source coding harness built on a Recursive Language Model (RLM) framework that rewrites its own prompts, memory, tasks and scaffolding at runtime based on failures. Opus 5 alone scores 30% on ARC-AGI-3; with the harness, 95.5%, a hair over the 95.4% human baseline. The real story is test-time compute and self-modifying scaffolding.
takeaways: Harness design can triple benchmark scores without a new model.
Let scaffolding adapt to observed failures at runtime.
A 0.1% margin over human baseline is noise, not superhuman.

title: Fully synthetic AI creator — Higgsfield, ElevenLabs, Veo and CapCut stack
summary: How viral fake-influencer videos are made: generate the character in Higgsfield or Midjourney, voice it with ElevenLabs, animate with an AI video model like Veo or Runway, and stitch in CapCut. Useful as a pipeline map and as a detection primer.
takeaways: Character image, voice, animation and edit are four separable stages.
Viral footage can now be fully synthetic; verify sources.

title: Kronos — transformer that reads candlesticks as a language (part 3)
summary: Final part of a Kronos explainer: after binary spherical quantization and hierarchical encoding turn candles into tokens, a transformer uses self-attention (query/key/value per candle) to weight relevant bars like a volume spike over chop, and an autoregressive decoder predicts the next tokens, i.e. future price action. Contrasts with sequential LSTMs.
takeaways: Tokenize OHLCV candles, then forecast with an autoregressive transformer.
Attention lets the model weight distant but relevant bars.
Open model you can test on your own markets.

title: Trojan-horse marketplace — co-marketing with adjacent vendors via AI
summary: Growth tactic from a former YC head of growth: have an AI app builder (Emergent) spin up a marketplace, find vendors selling to the same customers (not direct competitors), invite them to be featured, offer generous affiliate splits (10% to you, 20% to them), and use the relationship to land co-branded webinars and channel partnerships.
takeaways: A directory is a low-friction excuse to open partner conversations.
Over-generous referral splits buy goodwill and co-marketing.

title: Gemma Translator — offline speech translation on a Raspberry Pi 5
summary: Google open-sourced Gemma Translator: Moonshine for speech recognition, Gemma for translation and a TTS model for voice, all on a Raspberry Pi 5 with no network at ~7 tokens/sec, enough for live Spanish–Mandarin conversation. Repo includes code, parts list (battery, touchscreen, speaker, micro keyboard with language knob), deployment script and printable STL case.
takeaways: Full speech-to-speech translation fits on a Pi with no cloud.
Complete BOM and STL files make it a weekend build.
~7 tok/s is enough for conversational latency.

title: Liquid Death concert placements — AI-automated band seeding playbook
summary: Recreates Liquid Death's stunt with AI: list venues in a city, every band playing in the next two weeks into a table, generate can-friendly album art for custom-printed boxes, and mail bands free product so the can sits on stage in every photo. Address-finding step raises privacy concerns.
takeaways: Seed products where cameras already are: stages, events.
Personalized packaging boosts the odds bands use it.
Contact bands via management, not home addresses.

title: Sherlock — install and run the top username OSINT tool with uv
summary: Install Sherlock in three commands: create and activate a venv with uv, then uv pip install sherlock-project; run sherlock followed by one or more usernames to find matching accounts across the web.
takeaways: uv venv + uv pip install sherlock-project gets you running fast.
Pass multiple usernames in one run.

title: Flock plate-search transparency site — see which police searched you and why
summary: A public website lets you enter a license plate and see which police departments ran Flock ALPR searches on it, browse a department's full search history, and read stated reasons (protest, theft, speeding). Flock reportedly sought a takedown that Cloudflare refused. Link gated behind a comment.
takeaways: ALPR audit logs reveal how plate searches are justified.
Search reasons like 'protest' show surveillance scope.

title: Trending Claude resource repo — unnamed 60k-star collection
summary: Teaser for a #1-trending GitHub repo (60k+ stars) collecting ready-made instructions, multi-step chains and a daily-updated feed of what top AI builders do; the repo isn't named in the post.
takeaways: Repo name gated; nothing to act on directly.
Reusable instruction files and chained steps are the ideas worth borrowing.

title: Open-source object tracking — the tech inside Flock cameras, free
summary: Repo Heist episode arguing the tracking behind $3k Flock cameras is free on GitHub: a 50k-star open-source library that detects, tracks and counts objects on any feed (doorbell, webcam, drone), demoed tracking every football player's speed, position and possession in one Python file. Repo name gated.
takeaways: Detection + tracking + counting is commodity open-source tech.
Sports analytics demos show the same stack.

title: Three OSINT tools — email account discovery, onion crawler, lookup suite
summary: Teaser for three OSINT tools: one maps an email to every account it signed up for with name, photo and breach data; one crawls every site linked from an onion address into a searchable file; one bundles 20 terminal lookups (phone, Wi-Fi location, crypto wallet tracing, Sherlock). Names gated.
takeaways: Check your own email's account and breach exposure.
Onion crawling to a searchable file avoids manual browsing.

title: DeepSeek V4 Flash re-post-training — big agentic gains, same model size
summary: DeepSeek re-post-trained V4 Flash (284B MoE, ~13B active) with no size or architecture change, jumping Terminal Bench 2.1 from 61.8 to 82.7, past the V4 Pro preview and near Claude Opus 4.8, at $0.28 per million output tokens. V4's original recipe distilled 10+ specialist teacher models; V4 Pro (rumored 1.6T, 49B active) is next.
takeaways: Post-training alone can transform agentic ability.
Cheap MoE models are closing on frontier agent benchmarks.
Applies to the API model only, not the web/app.
